title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 15
paragraphs: The Paeonians, learning that the Persians were coming against them, gathered all their forces together and marched out toward the sea, supposing that when the Persians invaded them they would make their attack from that side. So the Paeonians were prepared, as I say, to drive off Megabazus's army when it came against them; but the Persians, hearing that the Paeonians had gathered their forces and were guarding the pass toward the sea, took guides and directed their course along the upper road; and passing unnoticed by the Paeonians, they fell upon the cities, which had been left without men, and finding them undefended easily took possession of them. When the Paeonians heard that their cities were in enemy hands, they at once dispersed, each tribe to its own place of habitation, and proceeded to hand themselves over to the Persians. So it was that these Paeonian tribes—the Siropaeones, the Paeoples, and all the others up to Lake Prasias—were removed from their homeland and taken to Asia.
